subject: Arabic
board: Pearson Edexcel Level 1/Level 2 GCSE (9-1) in Arabic (1AA0)
source: Gap-fill against Pearson Edexcel GCSE Arabic 1AA0 specification

lessons.title: School subjects: favourites, hardest and most useful
lessons.bigQuestion: Which subjects matter most to me, and why?
objectives: Give opinions with reasons about subjects
Use comparatives and superlatives for subjects
successCriteria: All: say your favourite subject and why
Most: say which subject is hardest or easiest
Some: compare two subjects and explain which is more useful
starter: Retrieval: say 'I go to school by bus'.
Retrieval: say the school day starts at eight.
Retrieval: say 'I like football because it is fun'.

teach.heading: Subjects
teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Revise any subjects pupils know and teach the rest. Note that الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ and الْعُلُومُ are plural in form: agreement is treated in the sentences below. Use only what pupils study. The subject list is for recognition and use in speaking.

teach.heading: Opinions and reasons
bullets: مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ هِيَ الْعُلُومُ - my favourite subject is science
لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ وَمُفِيدَةٌ - because it is enjoyable and useful
لَا أُحِبُّ التَّارِيخَ لِأَنَّهُ مُمِلٌّ - I do not like history because it is boring
أَسْتَمْتِعُ بِدَرْسِ الْفَنِّ - I enjoy the art lesson
teach.note: Teach لِأَنَّهَا for a feminine subject, لِأَنَّهُ for a masculine one (التَّارِيخُ). Ask pupils to check the pronoun matches the noun. Teach أَسْتَمْتِعُ بِ (I enjoy). Encourage varied opinions, not only 'like' and 'dislike'.

teach.heading: Hardest, easiest, most useful

left.title: Superlative
points: أَصْعَبُ مَادَّةٍ بِالنِّسْبَةِ لِي هِيَ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ - the hardest subject for me is maths
أَسْهَلُ مَادَّةٍ هِيَ الْفَنُّ - the easiest subject is art

right.title: Comparative
points: الْعُلُومُ أَكْثَرُ فَائِدَةً مِنَ الْفَنِّ - science is more useful than art
التَّارِيخُ أَصْعَبُ مِنَ الْجُغْرَافْيَا - history is harder than geography

teach.note: Superlative = أَفْعَلُ + indefinite singular noun (أَصْعَبُ مَادَّةٍ). Comparative = أَفْعَلُ + مِنْ. أَصْعَبُ and أَسْهَلُ are diptotes (no tanwin). Note أَكْثَرُ فَائِدَةً for 'more useful' as a pattern for adjectives that do not take أَفْعَلُ. Higher-tier work should use both.

teach.heading: Model: my subjects

model.problem: Write: 'My favourite subject is science because it is enjoyable. The hardest subject for me is maths. Science is more useful than art.'
steps: 'My favourite subject is science' = مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ هِيَ الْعُلُومُ
'The hardest subject for me is maths' = أَصْعَبُ مَادَّةٍ بِالنِّسْبَةِ لِي هِيَ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ
'Science is more useful than art' = الْعُلُومُ أَكْثَرُ فَائِدَةً مِنَ الْفَنِّ
model.answer: مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ هِيَ الْعُلُومُ لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ. أَصْعَبُ مَادَّةٍ بِالنِّسْبَةِ لِي هِيَ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ. الْعُلُومُ أَكْثَرُ فَائِدَةً مِنَ الْفَنِّ.

teach.note: Highlight that العلوم takes a feminine singular pronoun (لِأَنَّهَا) in this sentence. Arabic specialist to check the agreement choices and diptote endings. In Arabic exams, vowelling is not expected, so also show the unvowelled version.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which sentence means 'Maths is harder than history'?
check.why: أَصْعَبُ مِنَ places maths first. B means 'the hardest subject', C reverses the comparison, D is ungrammatical.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Ask which word means 'than' (مِنْ). If pupils choose C, check who is being compared with whom.

teach.heading: Knowledge as a value

quote.source: Qur'an, Surat Ta-Ha 20:114 (Arabic specialist to check the text)

bullets: رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا - my Lord, increase me in knowledge
الْعِلْمُ يَنْفَعُنِي - knowledge benefits me
teach.note: Use the ayah as a moment of reflection, not a translation task. Link to why studying even the hardest subject is worthwhile. Verify the reference with an Arabic or Islamic studies colleague before use.

practice: Say your favourite subject and give a reason.
Say which subject is hardest for you.
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about your subjects, with opinions and reasons.
Extend: add a comparative and a superlative.
Stretch: write 100 words: 'Which subjects will help my future?'
exit: Write your favourite subject and one reason.
Write one comparison between two subjects.
lessons.homework: Write 90 words in Arabic about your timetable and your opinions of each subject.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: subject picture cards and sentence frames. Stretch: use the pattern أَكْثَرُ ... مِنْ and a relative clause.

lessons.unit: Unit 4.1: Using languages beyond the classroom
lessons.title: Arabic for travel and for work
lessons.bigQuestion: How could Arabic help me when I travel and in a future job?
objectives: Explain how languages help when travelling
Explain how languages help in employment
Use conditional sentences and the future
successCriteria: All: say one way Arabic helps when travelling
Most: say one way it helps in a job
Some: use إِذَا ... فَ to link languages and future plans
lessons.smsc: Cultural: respecting people through their language
starter: Retrieval: say 'I speak English and a little Arabic'.
Retrieval: say 'I want to visit Cairo'.

teach.heading: Arabic when travelling
bullets: أَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَ السُّكَّانِ - I talk with the locals
أَسْأَلُ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ - I ask about the way
أَفْهَمُ الْقَائِمَةَ - I understand the menu
أَتَعَرَّفُ عَلَى ثَقَافَةٍ جَدِيدَةٍ - I get to know a new culture
teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Ask pupils if they have used Arabic while travelling. Note مَعَ and عَنْ after the verbs. Qur'an 49:13 speaks of peoples and tribes made so that they may know one another (verify the reference and wording before quoting). Keep pupil experience central.

teach.heading: Arabic at work
teach.note: These are masculine forms; add taa marbuta for a woman (مُتَرْجِمَةٌ, مُرْشِدَةٌ). Idāfa structure for the last two: first noun has no al-, last noun carries al-. Ask which of these jobs could use two languages.

teach.heading: Why languages matter
bullets: الشَّرِكَاتُ تَبْحَثُ عَنْ مُوَظَّفِينَ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ لُغَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً - companies look for staff who speak many languages
إِتْقَانُ لُغَةٍ ثَانِيَةٍ مَيْزَةٌ - mastering a second language is an advantage
اللُّغَاتُ تَفْتَحُ فُرَصًا جَدِيدَةً - languages open new opportunities
teach.note: Relative clause after an indefinite noun has no relative pronoun: مُوَظَّفِينَ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ. Point out the plural of the participle (مُوَظَّفُونَ becomes مُوَظَّفِينَ after عَنْ). Link to the pupils' own plans. Teach 'because' and 'advantage' words for writing.

teach.heading: Model: future plans

model.problem: Write: 'If I speak Arabic well, I will be able to work in a hotel in Cairo. I want to be a tour guide.'
steps: 'If I speak Arabic well' = إِذَا تَكَلَّمْتُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ جَيِّدًا
'I will be able to work' = فَسَأَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْمَلَ
'in a hotel in Cairo' = فِي فُنْدُقٍ فِي الْقَاهِرَةِ
'I want to be a tour guide' = أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مُرْشِدًا سِيَاحِيًّا
model.answer: إِذَا تَكَلَّمْتُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ جَيِّدًا فَسَأَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْمَلَ فِي فُنْدُقٍ فِي الْقَاهِرَةِ. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مُرْشِدًا سِيَاحِيًّا.

teach.note: A past-form verb after إِذَا has a future meaning. After أَنْ the verb ends in -a (أَعْمَلَ, أَكُونَ). After كَانَ/يَكُونُ the predicate is accusative (مُرْشِدًا سِيَاحِيًّا). Arabic specialist to check.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: What does إِذَا تَكَلَّمْتُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ فَسَأَعْمَلُ مُتَرْجِمًا mean?
options: If I speak Arabic, I will work as a translator
I spoke Arabic and worked as a translator
I never speak Arabic as a translator
When I worked, I spoke Arabic
check.why: إِذَا + past verb signals a future condition, and سَأَعْمَلُ is future. B and D are real past, C is wrong.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Many pupils will translate the first verb as past; remind them of the conditional form.

practice: Say one way Arabic helps when you travel.
Name one job that uses languages.
Translate: 'I want to work as a translator in the future.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about using languages when travelling and at work.
Extend: add a conditional sentence with إِذَا.
Stretch: write 100 words: 'Arabic and my future'.
exit: Write one job where a second language helps.
lessons.homework: Write 90 words in Arabic about how languages could help you in a future job.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: job picture cards and sentence frames. Stretch: add two reasons with لِأَنَّ and a conditional.

lessons.title: Volunteering and training: giving time and gaining skills
lessons.bigQuestion: How do volunteering and training help me and other people?
objectives: Talk about volunteering and who it helps
Use past tense and future tense to describe experience and plans
successCriteria: All: say one place you volunteer or could volunteer
Most: say what you did or will do and what you learn
Some: explain how volunteering and training lead to ambitions
lessons.smsc: Moral and social: serving others (khidma) and community support
starter: Retrieval: say 'I want to study engineering'.
Retrieval: say 'I helped my mother yesterday'.
Retrieval: say 'I will go to university'.

teach.heading: Volunteering

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: I will volunteer in the summer

teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Use real examples (masjid, food bank, charity shop). The believers are like a building, each part strengthening the other (Bukhari and Muslim): a paraphrase to use in discussion. Note الْمُحْتَاجِينَ is a plural participle in the accusative.

teach.heading: Training and skills
bullets: أَخَذْتُ دَوْرَةً فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ - I took a first-aid course
أَكْتَسِبُ خِبْرَةً وَمَهَارَاتٍ - I gain experience and skills
التَّدْرِيبُ يُسَاعِدُنِي عَلَى إِيجَادِ وَظِيفَةٍ - training helps me find a job
teach.note: Teach أَخَذْتُ دَوْرَةً (I took a course). Note فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ (first aid). The masdar إِيجَادِ follows عَلَى. Ask pupils what training they might choose: first aid, coding, languages, sport coaching. Use real options.

teach.heading: Model: what I did and what I learnt

model.problem: Write: 'Last summer I volunteered at a charity. I learnt new skills. Next year I will take a first-aid course.'
steps: 'Last summer I volunteered' = الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ تَطَوَّعْتُ
'I learnt new skills' = تَعَلَّمْتُ مَهَارَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً
'Next year I will take a first-aid course' = فِي السَّنَةِ الْقَادِمَةِ سَآخُذُ دَوْرَةً فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ
model.answer: الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ تَطَوَّعْتُ فِي جَمْعِيَّةٍ خَيْرِيَّةٍ. تَعَلَّمْتُ مَهَارَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً. فِي السَّنَةِ الْقَادِمَةِ سَآخُذُ دَوْرَةً فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ.

teach.note: Three-tense writing: past, past, future. Note the adverbial accusative الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ (last summer). Pupils who add a reason with لِأَنَّ move up the mark scheme. Arabic specialist to check the future form سَآخُذُ.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which sentence means 'I will volunteer in the summer'?
check.why: سَـ gives the future. B is past, C is a habit and D is 'I will not'.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Ask pupils to underline the future marker.

practice: Say where you volunteer or could volunteer.
Translate: 'I will take a training course next year.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about volunteering and training.
Extend: add what you learnt and a future plan.
Stretch: write 100 words: 'How volunteering and training prepare me for work'.
exit: Write one place you could volunteer.
Write one thing training gives you.
lessons.homework: Write 90 words in Arabic about volunteering you have done or would like to do.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: matching cards for activities and skills; sentence frames. Stretch: add a conditional and a relative clause.

lessons.title: Jobs, careers and professions
lessons.bigQuestion: What job might I do in the future, and why?
objectives: Talk about careers, hours and pay
Explain a future career using أُرِيدُ أَنْ and reasons
successCriteria: All: say what job someone does
Most: say what job you want and why
Some: compare two careers and justify a choice
lessons.smsc: Moral: honest earning and dignity of work
starter: Retrieval: say 'I study at secondary school'.
Retrieval: say 'my father works in a shop'.
Retrieval: say 'I want to go to university'.

teach.heading: Jobs and professions
teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Pupils choose professions that interest them. Show how the feminine is formed with taa marbuta. Arabic names for jobs often follow the pattern مُفَعِّل or فَاعِل: ask pupils to spot it. Revise from earlier jobs lesson but go beyond it.

teach.heading: Describing a job
bullets: أَبِي يَعْمَلُ مُحَاسِبًا - my father works as an accountant
الْوَظِيفَةُ بِدَوَامٍ جُزْئِيٍّ - the job is part-time
سَاعَاتُ الْعَمَلِ طَوِيلَةٌ - the working hours are long
الرَّاتِبُ جَيِّدٌ - the salary is good
teach.note: After يَعْمَلُ the job is accusative (مُحَاسِبًا): this is an accusative of state. Ask pupils to say what their parents or relatives do, only if they are comfortable. Discuss the pros and cons: hours, pay, helping people. The Prophet said that no food is better than what a man eats from the work of his own hand (Bukhari).

teach.heading: My career

left.title: My ambition
points: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مُهَنْدِسًا - I want to be an engineer
أُفَضِّلُ وَظِيفَةً تُسَاعِدُ النَّاسَ - I prefer a job that helps people

right.title: Reasons
points: لِأَنَّ الرَّاتِبَ جَيِّدٌ - because the salary is good
وَلِأَنَّنِي أُحِبُّ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ - and because I like maths

teach.note: After لِأَنَّ the next noun is accusative (الرَّاتِبَ). With a pronoun, لِأَنَّنِي. The relative clause after an indefinite noun has no الَّذِي: وَظِيفَةً تُسَاعِدُ. Pupils write two ambitions with reasons.

teach.heading: Model: my career

model.problem: Write: 'I want to be a doctor because I like helping people. The job is hard but the salary is good. I will study medicine at university.'
steps: 'I want to be a doctor' = أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا
'because I like helping people' = لِأَنَّنِي أُحِبُّ مُسَاعَدَةَ النَّاسِ
'The job is hard but the salary is good' = الْوَظِيفَةُ صَعْبَةٌ وَلَكِنَّ الرَّاتِبَ جَيِّدٌ
'I will study medicine at university' = سَأَدْرُسُ الطِّبَّ فِي الْجَامِعَةِ
model.answer: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا لِأَنَّنِي أُحِبُّ مُسَاعَدَةَ النَّاسِ. الْوَظِيفَةُ صَعْبَةٌ وَلَكِنَّ الرَّاتِبَ جَيِّدٌ. سَأَدْرُسُ الطِّبَّ فِي الْجَامِعَةِ.

teach.note: Notice وَلَكِنَّ with a noun in the accusative (الرَّاتِبَ). A pupil may use وَلَكِنْ with a nominative noun: both are accepted in standard Arabic. Female pupils say طَبِيبَةً. Arabic specialist to check.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: What does أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مُهَنْدِسَةً mean?
options: I (female) want to be an engineer
I (male) want to be an engineer
I will not be an engineer
check.why: مُهَنْدِسَةً has taa marbuta, so the speaker is female. B has the masculine form, C is past and D is negative.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Ask pupils to circle the feminine marker.

practice: Say what job your relative does.
Say what job you want and one reason.
Translate: 'The job is part-time and the salary is good.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about a job you would like to do.
Stretch: write 100 words comparing two careers and choosing one.
exit: Write the Arabic for 'I want to be a nurse'.
Write one advantage of a job.
lessons.homework: Write 90 words in Arabic about your future career.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: job cards with pictures and sentence frames. Stretch: add a conditional and relative clause.
